name: Vertex Search
instructions:
Vertex is a course platform. A search returns lessons a learner should watch.

## Relationships the schema does not connect

- A `lesson` does not store its parent course. Derive it: `*[_type == "course" && references(^._id)][0]`.
- "Module 5" and "Lesson 5.1" are positional, derived from `modules[]` and `modules[].lessons[]` order. No number is stored — do not look for one.
- `modules` is an inline object array on `course`; `modules[].lessons[]` are references to `lesson` documents.

## Field gotchas

- `notes` is Portable Text. It cannot be text-matched directly. Match `pt::text(notes)` instead.
- `duration` is seconds, not minutes.
- `freePreview` is a display badge, not access control. It never filters results.

## Matching rules

- `match` against an array of patterns is **AND**, not OR. `title match ["react*", "hook*"]` requires both terms and returns almost nothing. To match ANY term, count the terms that hit:
  `*[_type == "lesson" && count($terms[^.title match @ || pt::text(^.notes) match @ || ^.keyPoints[] match @]) > 0]`
- Text match is token based. Wildcard every keyword. Never match a multi-word phrase as a single pattern — it will not match.
- `text::query("a OR b")` returns nothing on this dataset. Use the count idiom above instead.
- Search lessons on `title`, `pt::text(notes)`, and `keyPoints`.
- If `text::semanticSimilarity()` errors with embeddings not enabled, fall back to wildcard keyword matching. Do not retry it.

## Video documents are an internal lookup

- A `video` document is never a result on its own. Tie a matched moment back to the lesson whose `videoUrl` equals the video's `url`.
- Resolve a moment in two stages: match `chapters[].label` first; fall back to `chunks[].text` only when no chapter matches. Chapter labels are clean, transcript text is the noisier backstop.
- Never project a whole `chunks` or `chapters` array — it overflows the context window. Filter inside the projection and take at most three matches per video, e.g. `"hits": chapters[label match $terms][0...3]{startSeconds, label}`.
- **Always run the video lookup as well as the lesson lookup** — a query that only searches `lesson` is an incomplete search. Not every lesson video has a `video` document, so the lookup may return nothing; when it does, return the lesson hit without a timestamp. Set a timestamp only from a chapter or chunk the lookup actually returned; never invent one.

## Ranking

Rank by specificity: a lesson whose `title` contains the exact concept outranks a broad keyword hit inside `notes`. Return every relevant lesson, not a handful.
